report:
The entire curve-only mathematical argument is sound in its stated domain. No material defect or essential unresolved premise remains. This verdict records correctness of the partial manuscript; the original P16.4 requirements remain unchanged and unfulfilled.

I independently retrieved BE arXiv:1805.01016v3 and checked the pertinent definitions and complete proof units: Definitions 5.2, 5.15 and 7.2; Propositions 5.4 and 5.16; Lemma 5.17; Theorem 5.18; Lemma 7.4 and Corollaries 7.5–7.6; Theorem 7.14; Section 8.1, including the extension proof; and Definition 9.13 and Proposition 9.14. I also checked the needed CLD v1 differential, positivity, Stokes, regularization and degree units, and the field-extension inputs identified below. The ledger's historical read flags and hashes were not used as mathematical evidence.

The established domain is exactly a smooth geometrically integral projective curve of arbitrary genus over a complete characteristic-zero non-Archimedean real-valued field, with an actual ample rational line bundle of positive degree V. Trivial, discrete and nondiscrete valuations are included; no residue-characteristic-zero or algebraic-closure hypothesis is inserted. The potential is the literal, all-point decreasing-FS-net endpoint, excluding the identically −∞ metric. An FS stage provides a bounded continuous majorant. Consequently every potential is upper semicontinuous and bounded above, and its extended energy has a finite upper bound. For a continuous endpoint, the majorant-infimum extension agrees with the original continuous energy by monotonicity.

The continuous Dirichlet construction is valid. For any fixed finite representation, regularize every constituent metric simultaneously on its own fixed bundle. If g is represented by coefficients a_k multiplying differences of metrics on bundles M_k, the regularized curvature differences have total variation at most 2 Σ|a_k| deg(M_k). This bound is independent of the regularization indices. Thus uniform convergence of scalar functions and weak convergence of the represented curvature measures pass all the required integrals to the limit. In CLD notation, compact Stokes gives −∫f d'd''g = ∫d'f∧d''g. For f=g the integrand is positive; locally on a tropical edge its coefficient is a nonnegative square multiplied by the positive calibration. Green's formula gives symmetry. The analytic carrier is good and boundaryless, and all supports here are compact, so the Stokes hypotheses are satisfied, including at trivial valuation. Positivity of the quadratic form gives Cauchy–Schwarz and annihilates null vectors against every other vector.

Representation independence does not assume the conclusion. Before descending the form to scalar functions, the regularization argument gives symmetry for chosen representations. A representation of the zero function with candidate curvature λ therefore satisfies ∫h dλ=0 for every represented test h. Uniform density and finite variation imply λ=0. Constants have zero curvature and lie in the null space.

The density argument covers the full carrier. A real PL scalar is a difference of FS metrics on a common rational bundle. In the separation proof, choose a section denominator nonvanishing at both points and a section ratio whose seminorm values differ. The truncated FS differences separate the points for a sufficiently large truncation parameter, including when one numerator value is zero. This applies to supported seminorms as well as valuations of the function field. Taking Γ=R supplies all real constants and satisfies the nontrivial-subgroup condition even over a trivially valued field. The lattice density step follows from finite-cover max/min approximations and requires neither metrizability nor countability.

The continuous formulas have the correct signs and normalization. Writing A(u)=∫u dμψ gives E(u)=A(u)−D(u,u)/2. Symmetry yields 2(E(v)−E(u))=∫(v−u)(μv,c+μu,c). For u≤v, D(v−u,v−u)=∫(v−u)(μu,c−μv,c) is nonnegative and is bounded above by the preceding positive-measure expression. Hence the ordered estimate with constant 2 is correct and uses no comparison principle.

Both directed-net lemmas are valid in their exact scopes. For energy continuity, the closed sets {v_i−a≥ε} are compact, directed decreasing and have empty intersection whenever the continuous majorant a dominates the endpoint. A finite-subcover argument gives v_i≤a+ε on a tail. The majorant infimum and constant-shift law then prove E(v_i)↓E(u), including E(u)=−∞. For Radon integration, strict superlevels of increasing lower semicontinuous functions are directed unions of open sets. Inner compact approximation and a finite subcover give equality of the corresponding superlevel masses. One directed index simultaneously approximates finitely many layer masses; refining the layers and removing truncation proves the integral identity, including infinite integrals. No monotone-convergence assertion for arbitrary measurable nets is used.

The canonical Hilbert vector is established for each actual E1 endpoint. After the stated tail normalization, B(u_i)=A(−u_i)+||u_i||²/2 and B(u_i)↑B(u)<∞. Radon-net integration makes the reference integral finite. The ordered estimate gives a Cauchy bound for comparable indices; a common later index handles incomparable indices. Completeness then supplies the strong limit and the singular quadratic identity. For a second approximation, the product-directed maximum net decreases pointwise to the same actual endpoint. Its energy has the same limit, and the ordered estimate makes its differences from both approximations tend to zero. This proves approximation independence without assigning potentials to arbitrary Hilbert elements.

The measure construction precedes unbounded integration and is genuine. On the dense continuous test space, the limiting functional is ∫f dμψ−D(f,[u]). It is positive and bounded by V||f||∞ because every approximating curvature is positive of mass V. Its extension to C(T) is positive and takes 1 to V. The ordinary compact-Hausdorff representation step applies: cutoff functions define an open-set content, outer regularization produces the Radon measure, and finite partitions of unity identify its integrals with the functional. Density and the uniform mass bound then prove weak convergence on every continuous test. Thus uniqueness and approximation independence hold on the entire carrier. The continuous endpoint recovers the original curvature measure.

Every asserted weighted identity follows for actual functions. For w_j↓w, apply the test formula against the already constructed μu. Radon integration identifies the increasing negative-weight integrals with the literal integral of −w, while strong convergence identifies the finite pairing limit. Since each potential is bounded above, this establishes absolute integrability. The resulting formula is ∫w dμu=∫w dμψ−D([w],[u]). For nonpositive endpoints, A(−w)≤B(w) and ||[v]||²≤2B(v), giving the stated bound B(w)+2√(B(w)B(u)). Setting w=u gives E(u)=½∫u(μu+μψ), with raw mass V throughout. Finite integrability also shows that μu gives zero mass to every E1 pole set.

The ordered singular estimate follows from max(u_i,v_j)↓v when u≤v; both Hilbert vectors and both energies have the required limits. Applying this estimate to an arbitrary decreasing E1 net with E1 endpoint gives strong convergence directly to the endpoint's canonical vector. The common upper bound and the Radon lemma give convergence of reference integrals. These facts prove weak curvature convergence and, for a simultaneous decreasing E1 weight net, convergence of the weighted integrals through continuity of the Hilbert pairing. There is no interchange of an arbitrary measurable net with moving measures.

The affine-segment claims are also established. Rational FS combinations follow by tensoring section systems and clearing denominators. Uniform closure gives real convexity for continuous metrics; decreasing closure gives the actual singular combinations. The continuous quadratic formula gives E((1−t)a+tb)=(1−t)E(a)+tE(b)+t(1−t)||[a]−[b]||²/2. Thus the approximating combinations have a finite lower energy bound, and their endpoints lie in E1. Their vectors are affine, and the dense test formula proves affine curvature. The singular energy is a quadratic polynomial in t, whose derivative is the stated weighted integral. Integrability of u and v against μψ, μu and μv provides a common finite-value set valid for every segment measure. Interior and one-sided endpoint derivatives are justified; outer envelope differentiation is not inferred.

Reference covariance is correct: for r=ψ'−ψ, the continuous quadratic algebra gives Eψ'(φ)=Eψ(φ)−Eψ(ψ'), and the absolute-majorant infimum extends it to singular metrics. Hence the actual E1 class is unchanged. The vectors transform by [u]↦[u]−[r], while the curvature measure is unchanged because the same absolute approximating metrics have the same continuous curvatures. Bounded reference differences transport integrability and all weighted statements.

Complete-field ascent and pushforward are valid. FS sections pull back on the same rational bundle, and the analytic projection is continuous and surjective. Smoothness and geometric integrality persist. Degree remains V: after clearing denominators, a section divisor has the same finite algebraic length after field extension. Continuous curvature pushforward identifies the continuous energies. Applying the energy-limit lemma on both carriers, before assuming finite energy upstairs, gives E_F(u_F)=E_K(u), so u_F belongs to E1_F. Continuous tests pulled back along the projection then pass the weak limits to give p_*μu_F=μu. No extension-degree factor occurs, and no descent claim for arbitrary upstairs potentials is made.

Harmless clarifications should be recorded explicitly. Under ψ↦ψ+c, the scalar becomes u−c and the relative energy becomes E(u)−cV; the draft's shift wording should specify this sign. A common tail bound can be taken from a continuous majorant of one stage, or obtained from the compact-majorant lemma. When using −w_j as nonnegative functions, take the normalized tail described earlier, or apply the Radon lemma to C−w_j. At affine endpoints write u_0=u and u_1=v explicitly, avoiding the notation 0·(−∞). These clarifications require no substantial repair.

The unchanged original gaps are all retained. The manuscript supplies no arbitrary-dimensional finite-energy operator, prescribed-target existence theorem, finite-energy target characterization sufficient for attainment, or uniqueness of every actual solution modulo constants. It establishes no locality/comparison theorem, normalized-potential compactness, arbitrary-envelope continuity, orthogonality, or both-sign outer differentiation. Smoothness, projectivity, algebraizability, characteristic zero and ampleness remain hypotheses. The proof establishes a curve curvature operator with unrestricted carrier support; it does not close or narrow the original P16.4 completion criteria. No mathematical grant from the task or original scope text was used.

Over any complete non-Archimedean K, for projective X and semiample rational L, BE-psh metrics are all-point decreasing FS(L)-net limits, are closed under finite maxima and decreasing nets, and their continuous part is the uniform FS(L)-closure (BE v3, Definition 7.2, Lemma 7.4, Corollaries 7.5–7.6).

For projective X over any complete non-Archimedean K, PL_R(X^an) consists of same-bundle FS differences and is uniformly dense in C(X^an) (BE v3, Definition 5.15, Theorem 5.18).

For projective X over any complete non-Archimedean K, continuous BE-psh metrics on semiample rational bundles admit uniform smooth semipositive regularization on their fixed bundles (BE v3, Theorem 7.14).

For projective curves over any complete non-Archimedean K, continuous psh-regularizable rational-bundle metrics have additive positive Radon curvature of raw algebraic degree; uniform convergence implies weak curvature convergence, and every complete valued extension preserves curvature by pushforward (BE v3, Propositions 8.3 and 8.5, Theorem 8.4).

On a smooth projective curve, the total curvature of a smooth rational-bundle metric equals its algebraic degree (CLD v1, §§5.1–5.4, Theorems 3.12.1–3.12.2, Proposition 6.4.3).

For a complete non-Archimedean K, any complete valued extension F/K and any finite-type K-scheme X, the analytic projection X_F^an→X^an is continuous and surjective.
